clue.text: She's in command in scene of Romeo and Juliet

indicators.note: the first in says one piece sits inside the other, the command abbreviation going into the city

parts.note: Shakespeare set the play in the Italian city of Verona
with the in before it, 'in command' gives IC, the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A woman takes charge on the set of a production of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's first 'in' does double duty: it is both the container signal and part of 'in command', the familiar abbreviation for in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so the pronoun 'She' stands for any woman so called.

clue.text: Seductive woman with passion joins club, being a nocturnal creature

parts.note: a vamp is a femme fatale
ire is anger, a strong passion
a bat is a club for hitting a ball

explanation.surface: A femme fatale, full of passion, signs up to a society for night owls.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood-feeding bat that flies and feeds at night, an animal active after dark.

clue.text: Knock back some elderberry wine

indicators.note: knock back, of a drink, here signals the letters being turned backwards
some means only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: Drink down a little homemade elderberry wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks DER from 'elderberry'; 'Knock back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a type of wine made from dark grapes, a familiar short name.

clue.text: Refusal to accept one old soldier's unworldliness

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a refusal
I is the Roman numeral one
vet is short for veteran, an old soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran's lack of sophistication shows in turning someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence or lack of experience, the quality of being unsophisticated.

clue.text: Gamblers in America who repeatedly miss the target?

definitions.meaning: players of the US dice game craps
people who are crap (bad) at shooting, taken literally

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful literal one: lousy marksmen.
explanation.definitionFit: In American dice, those who throw the dice in craps are its players.

clue.text: Give precise change, but without right coins

indicators.note: to change the word precise is to alter the order of its letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand over the exact money, but not in the correct coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tells you the R (right) is left over: the letters of PRECISE, less R, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in the form of coin rather than notes, a formal financial term.

clue.text: Orphan found by river under soft basket

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed below the preceding part

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
Little Orphan Annie is a famous American comic-strip orphan

explanation.surface: A parentless child is discovered by a river beneath a soft basket, Moses-style.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a large basket carried by a donkey or on a bicycle.

clue.text: Response is muted at first, after promoting Catholic opposition to Darwin?

indicators.note: promoting means moving up, so the letter is advanced to the front

parts.note: a reaction is a response

indicators.note: at first means take the first letter

explanation.surface: A muted response to elevating a Catholic in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: REACTION + IS + M (first of 'muted') makes REACTIONISM; 'promoting' moves its C to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The belief that God made the world as Genesis says, which rejects Darwin's evolution.

clue.text: The first female monarch in history

parts.note: in Genesis, Eve is the first woman
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A question of who was the first woman to reign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monarch' looks part of 'first female monarch', but it is R alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at any time, as in 'the best in history' = 'the best yet'.

clue.text: Wacky clothing almost entirely for a song

parts.note: wacky means mad, crazy
a rig is an outfit of clothes

indicators.note: almost means the synonym is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: entirely means all, wholly

explanation.surface: Crazy outfits almost wholly in aid of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' is ALL less its last letter, giving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices, a Renaissance vocal form.

clue.text: Belong essentially out there? The opposite

definitions.meaning: to be an inherent, intrinsic part of something
the opposite of out is in and of there is here, read as a two-word phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about belonging, then turning the phrase out there on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap each word of 'out there' for its opposite to get the second reading, IN HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to exist as an inseparable, intrinsic quality within something.

clue.text: All there is beneath rotting vegetation will overwhelm people

indicators.note: in a down answer, beneath places the second part below the first
overwhelm means engulf, so the other piece ends up inside

parts.note: compost is decaying plant matter
men means people

explanation.surface: Beneath the compost heap lies something that will swamp people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All there' is the colloquial phrase for mentally sound, not a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'of sound mind', meaning sane, which is the colloquial sense of all there.

clue.text: Monet, sir, is one case of painters styled as this

definitions.text: Monet, sir, is one case of painters styled as this

indicators.note: styled means fashioned or arranged, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words taken as written, except that one becomes I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the case, or outer shell, of a word is its first and last letters, here of the word painters

explanation.surface: Someone is told that Monet exemplifies a group of painters with a particular style.
explanation.walkthrough: MONETSIRIS plus I and PS (the outside of 'painters') are rearranged. The whole clue also defines: Monet is one case of painters of that style.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the leading figure of the French Impressionist movement in painting.

clue.text: Very steep prices put one off getting round in

indicators.note: off means wrong or gone bad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Steep price rises deter a person from shopping round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting round in' says O joins the mix: O goes into the scramble of PRICESPUT and I, which 'off' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitous means like a precipice: dangerously high or steep.

clue.text: Abandoned woman's going around with one having sinister tendency

parts.note: left means abandoned

indicators.note: going around means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: her is the female possessive
and means with, together

explanation.surface: A deserted woman takes up with someone of evil intent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' is Latin for left, so 'sinister tendency' is a leaning to the left hand, not wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister comes from the Latin for left, so a person favouring that side fits.

clue.text: Pieces penned by you once about adversary

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the assembly is read backwards
penned by means enclosed within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ye is the archaic plural form of you
chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Something written long ago, addressed to you, concerning a foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts the chessmen in the old pronoun, giving YMENE; 'about' then turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is a foe or opponent, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cracking working model's not quite perfect by design

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
to model is to pose; the 's reads as 'is' joining the parts

indicators.note: not quite says drop the last letter

parts.note: pure means perfect, flawless

explanation.surface: An excellent working model falls just short of perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite perfect' is PURE less its E, PUR, which cracks ON + POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something deliberately means acting intentionally, with intent rather than by accident.

clue.text: Cuts off a romance with prat

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful tales, to lie
prat is slang for the buttocks, whose Latin term is nates

explanation.surface: Someone ends a love affair with an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prat' is not the fool here but the bottom, British slang, giving NATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to estrange them, isolating them from you.

clue.text: Composer turning out Ring, a short work

indicators.note: turning out means expelling one letter and putting another in its place

parts.note: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A composer produces his Ring, a brief work, unlike Wagner's.
explanation.walkthrough: NOVELLO with its last O replaced by A.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a prose piece between story and novel.

clue.text: E.g. Wenceslas Square's shown by books on capital

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the piece before it

parts.note: S is taken as an abbreviation for square
capital, meaning excellent, is A1, written AI
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Prague's famous Wenceslas Square displayed in books about a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital as an adjective means first-rate, A1, written AI. Good King Wenceslas of the carol was canonised.
explanation.definitionFit: Wenceslas, Duke of Bohemia, was venerated as a holy martyr after his death and became the Czech patron.

clue.text: Salmon and lettuce served up — that has essential vitamin

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means written upwards

parts.note: cos is a type of lettuce
key means essential
E is a vitamin

explanation.surface: A salmon and salad dish, with a crucial vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: COS read upwards gives SOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sockeye is a red-fleshed Pacific species of this fish.

clue.text: Quote from tenor: "I'd never perform Butterfly"

indicators.note: perform is read as act on, working these letters into a fresh order

parts.note: the comma is a butterfly with a comma-shaped mark on its wing

explanation.surface: A tenor vows never to sing Madama Butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: T and IDNEVER are rearranged into INVERTED. 'Butterfly' looks like the opera but is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks are also called inverted commas, and 'quote' is short for one.

clue.text: Private bar in the Northward Arms

indicators.note: in a down answer, northward means read from bottom to top

parts.note: guns are arms

explanation.surface: A private bar in a pub called the Northward Arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' looks like part of a pub name, but it is weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug is a small, cosy room in a British pub.

clue.text: Turkey is something you eat

definitions.meaning: a turkey is a fool or flop
a strip of pasta eaten in soups and stir-fries

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' suggests food but its food sense is a decoy; it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is slang for a simpleton, and also a strip of pasta.

clue.text: Reversing round double bend, defects will be emphasised

indicators.note: reversing means the assembly is read from end to start
round means going about, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to defect is to desert
an S-bend is a double bend in a road or pipe

explanation.surface: A driver backing round an S-shaped curve finds the car's faults highlighted.
explanation.walkthrough: DESERTS round S makes DESSERTS, which 'Reversing' turns back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressed syllable or point is one given emphasis or weight.

clue.text: Find out either way

indicators.note: either way means it reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Discover something whichever way you go.
explanation.definitionFit: Sus or suss is informal British slang for discover or work out.

clue.text: Maybe Mahler bust a gut tackling start of Symphony 5

indicators.note: tackling means taking on, holding the next piece within
bust means broken, so these letters are scrambled
start of means the first letter only

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Mahler, perhaps, straining himself writing his fifth symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: A GUT is rearranged as GUTA, with S (start of 'Symphony') inside, then V.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler, the Austrian composer, is one example bearing this first name.

clue.text: Oil company's run by idiot, one judges

parts.note: an ass is a fool
Esso is a petrol brand; the 's reads as 'has'
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A petroleum firm is managed by a fool who passes judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates or appraises, someone whose job is to judge value or merit.
